parts:
Hello,

 

My apology for sending you earlier an incorrect attachment. Attached please see the forest plots.  Could someone give me hints or help me with the code that I need to add in order to have the OR and 95% CI printed under each geom_hline? I could send you the reprodicble code if needed.

 

Thanks,

 

Pradip Muhuri

 

 

 

 

p <- ggplot(data, aes(x=xcovariate_f, or,y=or, ymin=lc, ymax=uc))+

  geom_pointrange()+

  geom_hline(aes(x=0), lty=2) +

  facet_wrap(~ age_cat_f)+

  coord_flip()+

  xlab ("  ")+

  ylab("  ")+

 

  theme_bw() +

  theme(panel.grid.major=element_blank(),panel.grid.minor=element_blank())+

  theme(strip.text.x=element_text(),

        strip.background = element_rect(colour="black", fill='white')  )

 

  print(p)

I have made my forest plots (please see the attachment) using the code below. Could someone give me hints or help me with the code that I need to add in order to have the OR and 95% CI printed under each geom_hline?

I could send you the reprodicble code if needed.

 

Thanks,

 

Pradip Muhuri

 

 

##################################################################

p <- ggplot(data, aes(x=xcovariate_f, or,y=or, ymin=lc, ymax=uc))+
  geom_pointrange()+
  geom_hline(aes(x=0), lty=2) +
  facet_wrap(~ age_cat_f)+
  coord_flip()+
  xlab ("  ")+
  ylab("  ")+

  theme(panel.grid.major=element_blank(),panel.grid.minor=element_blank())+

Hi Ben and Dennis,

Per your advice, I am now sending you the reproducible example (appended below and also attached). I was trying to draw the forest plots for 11 covariates for each of two models by age groups. In the data set, OR =odds ratio, and the lc and uc = confidence interval limits.

As usual, Dennis has provided very useful guidance, suggesting two approaches. I am leaning toward his Approach 2. Although the R script (shown below) has run successfully, the plots are overshadowed with the character string that involves the OR and confidence limits. I was trying to insert the character string to the right side of each of the plot lines. It seems that my geom_text needs to be fixed (y-value, x-value, and hjust in the geom_text).

I would appreciate receiving your advice.

Thanks,

Pradip Muhuri

theme(panel.grid.major=element_blank(),panel.grid.minor=element_blank())+
theme(strip.text.x=element_text(),
strip.background = element_rect(colour="black", fill='white')
)

print(p)

messages.author: 942ffec526d6a312
messages.subject: Re: Adding OR and 95% CI to the forest plots- repost
parts: Hi Pradip,

> As usual, Dennis has provided very useful guidance, suggesting two approaches. I am leaning toward his Approach 2. Although the R script (shown below) has run successfully, the plots are overshadowed with the character string that involves the OR and confidence limits. I was trying to insert the character string to the right side of each of the plot lines. It seems that my geom_text needs to be fixed (y-value, x-value, and hjust in the geom_text).

I think this is doing pretty much what you want (removed geom_text from
your code, then played with it
separately):

p <- ggplot(data, aes(x=xcovariate_f, or,y=or, ymin=lc, ymax=uc))+
geom_pointrange()+
geom_hline(aes(x=0), lty=2) + facet_wrap(~ age_cat_f)+
coord_flip()+
xlab (" ")+
ylab(" ")+
theme_bw() +
theme(panel.grid.major=element_blank(),panel.grid.minor=element_blank())+
theme(strip.text.x=element_text(),
strip.background = element_rect(colour="black",
fill='white') )

p+geom_text(aes(label=string.est,y=uc),hjust=-0.02,colour="black",size=3)+
scale_y_continuous(limits=c(0,4.25))

Using uc to set the y coordinate is what you need to do if you want the
labels just to the right
of the line (ie different position for each label). I'm not sure that
looks very nice, so if you want
them at a constant position to the right of all the lines, then it is
just of case of setting the y
coordinate appropriately, eg:

p+geom_text(aes(label=string.est,y=max(uc)+0.1),hjust=-0.02,colour="black",size=3)+scale_y_continuous(limits=c(0,4.25))

The other things are just tweaks to adjust positions and size of the
text and to make
enough room in the plot for the labels.

You will want to play with the values a bit.

Ron.

Hello Ron,

Thank you so much for your guidance on the geom_text. I like your idea of setting the y coordinate at a constant position to the right of all lines.

Inserting your code renders the desired output only after now=3 is specified on the facet_wrap(). I could not make the code work without specifying nrow=3 on the facet_wrap(). Below are my questions:

1) What to tweak to make your code work without nrow=3 on the facet_wrap()?
2) What would I specify to change the orientation of the chart to landscape?
3) What is the best way to increase the font size globally?
4) Would you please explain to me how this code [y=max(uc)+0.1)] sets the y coordinate at a constant position?

I look forward to receiving your advice/hints.

Pradip

theme(strip.text.x=element_text(),
strip.background = element_rect(colour="black",
fill='white') )

p+geom_text(aes(label=string.est,y=uc),hjust=-0.02,colour="black",size=3)+
scale_y_continuous(limits=c(0,4.25))

Using uc to set the y coordinate is what you need to do if you want the
labels just to the right
of the line (ie different position for each label). I'm not sure that
looks very nice, so if you want
them at a constant position to the right of all the lines, then it is
just of case of setting the y
coordinate appropriately, eg:

p+geom_text(aes(label=string.est,y=max(uc)+0.1),hjust=-0.02,colour="black",size=3)+scale_y_continuous(limits=c(0,4.25))

The other things are just tweaks to adjust positions and size of the
text and to make
enough room in the plot for the labels.

You will want to play with the values a bit.

Ron.
